Md Mazibar Rahman, Advocate-For the Petitioner. 
Md Safed Ali, Assistant Attorney-General-For the Respondents.
parties:
Mahatab Hossain (Md) ------ Petitioner
vs
Upazila Nirbahi Officer and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. The petitioner being a citizen of Bangladesh was appointed “জীপ গাড়ীর ড্রাইভার” vide Memo No. 62 dated 28-4-1988 issued by the Chairman, Upazila Parishad, Pirganj, Rangpur (Annexure A) with effect from 12-4-1988 as per resolution No.3 dated 11-4-1988 of the said Parishad. Before joining the said post the petitioner was in the service of Mithapukur Upazila as driver and resigned from the said post on 20-10-1986 which was duly accepted by the Parishad as it appears from Memo No.705(4) 86 dated 2-12-1986 (Annexure A1). The respondent No.1 is the Upazila Nirbahi Officer of Pirgonj, Rangpur. The respondent No.2 is the Deputy Commissioner, Rangpur and the respondent No.3 is the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives, Local Government Division and the respondent No.4 is the Subordinate Officer of the respondent No.3. On 16-6-1993 the petitioner submitted an application praying for three days casual leave and having obtained the leave granted by the respondent No.1, the petitioner left the station for his village home and thereafter he fell ill and could not join his duties and accordingly, he prayed for extension of leave on medical ground by submitting as many as eight applications and after recovery from illness on 26-1-1994 he filed an application along with medical certificate for joining. On 26-1-1994 the respondent No.1 put his signature on an order being Memo No. 7911(4) (Annexure C) purported to have been issued by him on 25-1-1994 suspending the petitioner from service without providing him any opportunity to explain. The aforesaid suspension order was issued by the respondent No.1 under Rule 11(i) of the Government Servant (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985, although the said Rule was not applicable because of the fact that the Upazila Parishad Karmachari Chakuri Bidhimala, 1989 was in force and ignoring the said Bidhimala the impugned order of suspension was issued by the respondent No.1 most illegally, arbitrarily and malafide. Bidhi 2(1)(jha) provides that "appointing authority" means the Parishad and, as such, the respondent No. 1 has no authority to suspend the employee of the Parishad and the impugned order of suspension is ex facie illegal and of no legal effect. Thereafter, an inquiry was conducted by a one-man Enquiry Committee headed by Md Abdur Razzak, Assistant Director, Local Government, Rangpur who by Memo No. Shthal153 dated 30-3-1994 submitted a report to the respondent No.1. The copy of the said report was not served upon the petitioner. Subsequently, on the prayer of the petitioner on 1-12-1994 a copy of the same was supplied to him by Memo No. 1107 dated 20-12-1994 (Annexure D). By the aforesaid memo the allegations brought against the petitioner were not proved. Thereafter, on 20-11-1994 a 2nd show cause notice (Annexure E) was issued by the respondent No.1 after a long lapse of nine months. The petitioner submitted a reply on 31-12-1994 to the aforesaid show cause notice (Annexure F). The petitioner filed a case before the Administrative Tribunal, Bogra being AT Case No. 46 of 1999 against the order of suspension for reinstatement in service with effect from 25-4-1994. The petitioner not being a Government Servant the case was not maintainable in law and accordingly, the said case was dismissed by judgment and order dated 22-2-2003 passed by the Administrative Tribunal. The memo dated 14-2-2001 (Annexure H) was issued by the respondent No.2 directing the respondent No. 1 to withdraw suspension order of the petitioner immediately and dispose of the matter in accordance with the inquiry report submitted on 30- 3-1994. The respondent No.1 did not follow the direction given by the respondent No.2. Thereafter, memo dated 30-8-2001 (Annexure 1) was issued by the respondent No.3 directing the respondent No. 1 to withdraw the suspension order of the petitioner by disposing of the Departmental Proceedings. But no action was taken. The respondent No.1 by the Memo No. U-NIIPIRl2003/2055 dated 30-11-2003 (Annexure J) dismissed the service of the petitioner with immediate effect. Thereafter, on 27-1-2004 the petitioner submitted an appeal (Annexure K) to the respondent No. 3 against the aforesaid order of dismissal from service. The respondent No.3 by the order dated 1-4-2004 dismissed the appeal of the petitioner affirming the order of dismissal and the said order was communicated to the petitioner vide Memo No; স্থাসবি/উপ-১/প১/২০০০/৭৭(১)(৩) dated 3- 4-2004 (Annexure L). 

 4. The respondents contested the Rule by filing Affidavit-in-Opposition denying all the material allegations stated in the writ petition stating, inter alia, that the petitioner was appointed as "Jeep Driver" on 28-4-1988. The petitioner left his office before the application for leave was granted. His application for leave was not granted. It is not true that he joined the office with 8 (eight) letters supported by medical certificates. The respondent No.1 sent many letters to the local addresses of the petitioner and thereafter, a notice was published in the local newspaper asking him to join in his service but he did not join and subsequently the respondent No.1 as per provisions of the Service Rules, 1985 issued the memo dated 26-1-1994 (Annexure C) temporarily suspending the petitioner from service. The respondent No.1 was given powers vide Memo No. Thana/Pa-37/8/92/916 dated 31-10-1994 for issuing the dismissal letter against the petitioner. The inquiry report was served upon the petitioner on 20-12-1994 vide Memo No. 1107. The show cause notice was duly issued and served upon the petitioner. The action was taken against the petitioner as per provisions of the Rules and Regulations. After abolition of Upazila Parishad, the Upazila Nirbahi Officer was given power as a selection authority vide Memo No. ThanalPa-378/92/916 dated 31-10-1994 for dismissing the petitioner. The petitioner applied for casual leave on 15-6-1993 from 16-6-1993 to 18-6-1993 and though his application for leave was not granted he left the office. He was repeatedly asked to join in his office but he did not comply with the order rather, he sent a telegram to the authority without mentioning his address as well as medical certificate. The petitioner was absent in his office intentionally. The respondents published notification regarding the petitioner's absence in "The Daily Juger Alo" dated 28- 9-1993 and he was asked to join in his office and, as such, he was temporarily suspended with effect from 16-6-1993 and charged under section 3C of the Government Servants' (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985. The action has been taken against him under Memo No. 79/1(4) dated 25-1-1994. Thereafter, the Assistant Director, Local Government Division, investigated the matter under Memo No. Stha-Sha-5/9/42(2) dated 31-1-1994 issued by the Deputy Commissioner, Rangpur and submitted his report. Subsequently, on 31-8-1995 a decision was taken for further investigation by the "Upazila Co-ordination Committee". Thereafter, on 1-7-1998 vide Memo No. 581 a show cause notice was served upon him under Bidhi 53(1) (Ka) and (Kha) and Bidhi 53(2) (Kha) of the Upazila Parishad Karmachari Chakuri Bidhimala, 1989 and the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Pirganj was re- appointed as the Investigation Officer but he did not perform his duties due to his transfer and thereafter, on 14-6-1999 the petitioner filed a case being Administrative Tribunal Case No.46 of 1999 before the Administrative Tribunal, Bogra and the said case was dismissed as being not maintainable and subsequently, one Md Saidur Rahman, Assistant Commissioner (Land) was appointed as the Investigation Officer under Memo No.490(4) dated 3-6-2001 by the decision dated 30-5-2001 of the Upazila Development and Co-ordination Committee and accordingly, on 24-11-2001 the report was submit- ted wherein it was found that the petitioner had been guilty of negligence, misconduct, unauthorised absence for long time and engaged himself in other activities in neglecting official duty intentionally in violation of Bidhi 53 (2)(Ka) and (Kha) of the Upazila Parishad Karmachari Chakuri Bidhimala, 1989 and on the basis of the said report, the petitioner was dismissed from his service by maintaining all legal procedures and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 6. Mr Md Safed Ali, the learned Assistant Attorney-General, appearing for the respondents, submits that there is no illegality in the impugned order of suspension, dismissal and also the order passed by the respondent No.3 dismissing the appeal and, as such, no interference is called for by this Honble Court. He then submits that the respondents have taken all steps as per provisions of Upazila Parishad Karmachari Chakuri Bidhimala, 1989 and the petitioner was given enough opportunity of being heard but he did not comply with the provisions of law rather he violated the orders of the respondents and the respondent authority after proper investigation complied with the legal formalities as per provisions of the aforesaid Bidhimala, 1989 and rightly passed the order of dismissal dated 30-11-2003 (Annexure-J) and the respondent No.3, the appellate authority having considered the case of the petitioner rightly passed the impugned order dated 1-4-2004 dismissing the appeal and affirming the order of dismissal issued by the respondent No.1 and, as such, no interference is called for by this Hon'ble Court and the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 7. We have perused the writ petition, Affidavit-in-Opposition and Supplementary Affidavit-in- Opposition submitted by the respondent No.3 with Annexures. It appears that admittedly the suspension order was issued on 26-1-1994 (Annexure-C) by the respondent No.1 under the Rule 11 (1) of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985. Then Mr Md Saidur Rahman, Assistant Commissioner (Land) was appointed as the Investigation Officer under Memo No. 490(4) dated 3-6- 2001 by the decision dated 30-5-2001 of the Upazila Development and Co-ordination Committee and accordingly, the report was submitted on 24-11- 2001 finding that the petitioner was guilty. Admittedly, the charge was framed against the petitioner under Bidhi 53(2)(Ka) and (Kha) of the Upazila Parishad Karmachari Chakuri Bidhimala, 1989. Admittedly the petitioner being an employee of Pirgonj Upazila Parishad his service is governed by the Upazila Parishad Karmachari Chakuri Bidhimala, 1989 but on the mistaken view by memo dated 25-1-1994 he was suspended from his service with effect from 16-6-1993 under Rule 11 (1) of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985 and accordingly, the matter proceeded against the petitioner and challenging the order of suspension the petitioner filed a case before the Administrative Tribunal, Bogra which was dismissed as being not maintainable because the petitioner was employed under the Upazila Parishad. It appears that subsequently, the respondent No.1 by Memo No.714 dated 24-8-1998 (Annexure-IV-F) issued second show cause notice upon the petitioner asking him to show cause as to why he should not be dismissed from his service for misconduct and other illegalities for violation of Bidhi 53(1 )(ka) and (kba) and 53(2)(kba) and 54 (ka) and (kha) of the Bidhimala 1989. To our utter surprise it appears that two years after this show cause notice by Memo No. 490(4) dated 3-6-2001 Mr Md Abdur Razzak, Assistant Director, Local Government, Rangpur was appointed as the Investigation Officer by the Upazila Development and Co-ordination Committee under Bidhi 58(2)(ga) of the aforesaid Bidhimala and he was asked to submit his report within 15 days. On perusal of the Memo No.631 dated 24-11-2001 it appears that the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Pirganj submitted his report after five months from the date of his appointment. 

 8. As per Bidhi 58(8) in case of failure of the Parishad to take final decision within 180 days from the date the allegations against the accused person are known to him the accused person shall be deemed to have been automatically relieved of or exonerated from the allegations brought against him and, in such event, the person or persons who are responsible for such failure shall have to explain the reason therefor and if the explanation is not found satisfactory he or they may be proceeded against on charge of inefficiency under the relevant provisions of law. In the instant case, it appears that admittedly the petitioner is an employee of Upazila Parishad. Initially, charge was framed against him under section 3(b) and 3(c) of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985 and subsequently, by memo dated 24-8-1998 the respondent No. 1 was said to have issued a second notice (Annexure IV F) under the Upazila Parishad Karmachari Chakuri Bidhimala, 1989. 

 10. It is, therefore, abundantly clear that after the dissolution of the Upazila Parishad all the employees of the said Parishad have been working under the control of the Upazila Nirbahi Officer. But the respondent-Government has not placed the service of the employees of the Upazila Parishad under the Government. It is only a temporary measure by which all the employees of the dissolved Parishad will be acting under the direct control of the Upazila Nirbahi Officer who will be functioning as the appointing authority. For the aforesaid reasons we find that the order dated 25-1-1994 (Annexure-C) was issued wrongly under the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985 though the dis- missal order dated 30-11-2003 (Annexure-J) has, been issued under the Upazila Parishad Karmachari Chakuri Bidhimala, 1989. This shows that proceeding was started against the petitioner wrongly under the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985 but the order of dismissal passed under the Upazila Parishad Karmachari Chakuri Bidhimala, 1989 would not cure the illegality. In the memo dated 30-11-2003 reference was made about the Enquiry Report dated 24-11- 2001 submitted by the Investigation Officer stating that allegation of misconduct and fraud contrary to the provisions of Bidhi 54(ka) and (kha), Bidhi 53(1)(ka) and (kha) and Bidhi 53(2)(kha) have been proved beyond reasonable doubt. But at the same time in the said order of dismissal dated 30-11-2003 it has been stated that according to the aforesaid Enquiry Report the allegations against the petitioner having been proved beyond reasonable doubt the second show cause notice dated 24-8-1998 was issued. It con not be reconciled how the Enquiry Report dated 24-11-2001 would be the basis for the second show cause notice issued on 24-8-1998. This shows that the entire action has been taken against the petitioner without application of mind and in violation of the mandatory provisions of the Bidhimala,1989. Accordingly, we are of the view that all the proceedings against the petitioner have been taken with total non-application of mind on the part of the respondent No.1 and the outcome of the entire proceedings will be declared to have been made without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect for having failed to conclude the proceeding drawn against the petitioner within 180 days from the date of service of charge sheet as contemplated under Bidhi 58(8) of the aforesaid Bidhimala, 1989. 

 11. It appears that the respondent No. 1 issued Memo dated 25-1-1994 (Annexure-C) suspending the petitioner under Rule 11 () of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985 although the said Rules are not applicable in the case of the petitioner because of operation of the Upazila Parishad Karmachari Chakuri Bidhimala, 1989. But the One Man Enquiry Committee headed by the Assistant Director, Local Government, Rangpur conducted the enquiry and submitted its report on 17-3-1994 vide memo dated 30-3-1994. But subsequently, on the prayer of the petitioner it was supplied to him vide memo dated 20-12-1994. A second' show cause notice dated 20-11-1994 (Annexure E) was issued by the respondent No.1 after long lapse of 9 months. It appears that the petitioner has submitted a reply on 31-12-1994. The petitioner was given subsistence allowance irregularlyfrom 16-6-1993 to 31-12-1995. The petitioner was not given any subsistence allowance from 1-1-1996 and the enquiry was not conducted till 28-12-1996 when the respondent No.1 all on a sudden appointed the Assistant Commissioner (land), Pirganj as the Investigation Officer for the second time. The petitioner was not served with a copy of the Enquiry Report. Thereafter, on 9-7-1998 another show cause notice was issued upon the petitioner under the Upazila Parishad Karrnachari Chakuri Bidhimala,1989. But without holding an enquiry another second show cause notice was issued upon the petitioner under Bidhi 54 of the aforesaid Bidhimala, 1989'on 24-8-1998. The petitioner filed written explanation. Then, another three-member Enquiry Committee was constituted by Memo No.1149 dated 14-12-1998 to enquire into the matter while the Enquiry Committee was very much in existence, another one-member Enquiry Committee was appointed on 4-5-1999 to enquire and report. The enquiry was conducted without submission of any report. But again, by order dated 17-5-1999 the petitioner was asked to appear before the Enquiry Committee on 15-6-1999. The petitioner filed written explanation on 27-7-1998 and 13-1-1999. Having received no decision for long 6 years and no subsistence allowance since 1-1-1996 the petitioner filed an appeal for redress before the Secretary, Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives on 4-1-1999. Thereafter, on 5-4-1999 the petitioner gave a reminder for disposal of the appeal. Having received no decision on the appeal the petitioner mistakenly filed a case being AT Case No.46 of 1999 before the Administrative Tribunal Bogra on 19-11-1999 for cancellation of the suspension order dated 25-1-1994 (Annexure-E) and to reinstate him in the service with back salaries from 16-6-1993. The case was contested by the respondent No.1. The Administrative Tribunal, Bogra by the judgment and order dated 24-2-2000 dismissed the case as not being maintainable because the petitioner was not a Government Servant rather he was employed by the Upazila Parishad, an autonomous statutory body. It appears that the respondent No.2 by Memo dated 14-2-2001 directed the respondent No.1 to withdraw the suspension order of the petitioner and dispose of the matter in accordance with the enquiry report submitted on 30-3-1994. But the respondent No. 1 did not follow the direction. Thereafter, the respondent No. 3 directed the respondent No.1 to dispose of the matter expeditiously but no action was taken. Rather, the respondent No.1 by order dated 30-11-2003 dismissed the service of the petitioner. Thereafter, the petitioner submitted an appeal to the respondent No.3 against the order of dismissal from service. The respondent No. 3 by order dated 1-4-2004 (Annexure-L) dismissed the appeal. 

 13. After more than four years, on 9-7-1998, allegation was raised against the petitioner asking him to show cause under the Upazila Parishad Karmachari Chakuri Bidhimala,1989. Again, the second show cause notice was issued on 24-8-1998 without holding any enquiry. Thereafter, series of Enquiry Committees were constituted to hold enquiry and finally Enquiry Committee was constituted on 4-5-1999. Though enquiry was held yet no report was submitted. In the compelling circumstances, the petitioner filed a representation before the Secretary to the concerned Ministry for not disposing of the Departmental proceeding for more than 6 years and for not making any payment in respect of subsistence allowance. He filed a reminder before the Secretary to the concerned Ministry. Finding no other alternative, he mistakenly filed a case before the Administrative Tribunal, Bogra. It is true that the case was dismissed by the Administrative Tribunal on the ground of maintainability since the petitioner was not employed by the Government but by the Upazila Parishad. 

 14. So, it appears that the entire proceedings against the petitioner was proceeded with total non- application of mind on the part of the respondents. It is the case of the respondents that the petitioner has committed misconduct which measures major punishment and proper action against the petitioner is required to be taken in accordance with the provisions of the Upazila Parishad Karmachari Chakuri Bidhimala, 1989. They are not required to invoke the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985 to take action against the petitioner. Bidhi 63 of the Bidhimala 1989 enumerates the relevant provisions of appeal which reads as follows: 

 15. Upa-Bidhi (2) of Bidhi 63 enjoins that the Appellate Authority will consider (a) whether the procedures prescribed by the Bidhimala have been followed or not and in case of non-compliance with the prescribed procedures whether justice has been denied to the petitioner, (b) whether the decisions given on the allegations is in accordance with law, (c) whether the penalty imposed is excessive, adequate or inadequate. 

 16. Bidhi 63(3) provides that the appeal is required to be disposed of by the Government within 90 days from the date of its filing after considering the grounds envisaged in Upa Bidhi (2) of Bid hi 63. But, in the instant case, it appears from the order of dismissal of appeal dated 1-4-2004 (Annexure-L) that the Appeal Authority failed to comply with the aforesaid provisions of Bidhi 63 in not finding that the procedures prescribed by the Bidhimala 1989 have not been followed rather the petitioner was suspended by order dated 25-1-1994 under the provisions of Rule 11 (1) of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985. The procedures envisaged in Bidhimala were not followed in disposing of the Departmental proceedings, rather the respondent No. 1 acted arbitrarily and illegally and the final order of dismissal dated 30-11-2003 was issued after a long lapse of about 10 years in violation of the provisions of Bid hi 58(8) of the Bidhimala 1989, which enjoins that final decision on the Departmental Proceedings should be made within 180 days from the date of serving the charge sheet upon the accused person, in default he shall be deemed to have been discharged automatically from the charge levelled against him. It appears that the Appeal was disposed of beyond the statutory period of 90 days from the date of filing of the Appeal in violation of the provisions of Bidhi 63(3) of the Bidhimala 1989. It also appears that the Appellate Authority failed to apply its mind in disposing of the petition of appeal filed by the petitioner. In that view of the matter the impugned order of dismissal dated 30-11-2003 (Annexure-J) and the order dated 1-4-2004 dismissing the Appeal (Annexure-J) passed by the appellate authority have been made without lawful authority.
